User-defined likelihood function for calibration

likelihood_function.Rd

Penalises simulated values that fall outside the [obs_lower, obs_upper] envelope defined in the observed data. Simulated values within the envelope incur no penalty; values below the lower bound or above the upper bound are penalised in proportion to the log-ratio of their deviation, scaled by 1e6 so the penalty dominates the objective function.

Usage

likelihood_function(obs, sim)

Arguments

obs

Numeric matrix or data frame with two columns: column 1 is the lower bound (obs_lower) and column 2 is the upper bound (obs_upper) of the observed data envelope. One row per time step or observation.

sim

Numeric vector of simulated values, one entry per row of obs.

Value

A non-negative numeric scalar. Returns 0 when all simulated values lie within their respective [obs_lower, obs_upper] bounds, and a large positive value otherwise (intended to be minimised as part of the calibration objective function).

Details

The penalty is computed as: $$-10^6 \sum \log\left(\min\left(\frac{s+1}{l+1}, 1\right)\right) + 10^6 \sum \log\left(\max\left(\frac{s+1}{u+1}, 1\right)\right)$$ where \(s\) is the simulated value, \(l\) the lower bound, and \(u\) the upper bound. Adding 1 to numerator and denominator avoids division by zero when values are near zero. NA values are ignored.

This function must be exported to cluster workers (e.g. via clusterExport) when running the calibration in parallel.

See also

min_max_likelihood

Examples

obs <- cbind(lower = c(10, 20, 30), upper = c(15, 25, 35))
sim <- c(12, 18, 40)   # 18 below lower[2], 40 above upper[3]
likelihood_function(obs, sim)
#> [1] 230136.6
